"Bonjour, Bridget," François said, his eyes twinkling with curiosity. "I must say, I'm astonished by your nation's sudden about-face. After all the belligerent bluster, it seems Britain has abruptly abandoned its aggressive ambitions."

"Astonishingly, François," Bridget replied, "our benevolent leader, Adolf Hitler, has proposed an alliance with Poland and Britain. It's a bold move, to say the least."

"Brilliantly, I suppose," François said, raising an eyebrow. "But what's behind this bizarre behavior? Has Britain been bewitched by the benevolent dictator's benevolence?"

"Cautiously, I've been investigating the matter," Bridget said, consulting a confidential document. "It appears Hitler has been secretly meeting with British officials, discussing a mutually beneficial agreement. Apparently, he's been impressed by Britain's audacious airpower and has proposed a joint alliance against the common enemy: communism."
